extracted.intended_audience: users of Mathematics Stack Exchange who are posting mathematical content (questions/answers/comments)
extracted.subtask_description: How to write and render mathematical notation on Mathematics Stack Exchange using LaTeX/MathJax, including inline vs block formulas and common symbol conventions. Focused guidance for composing posts that include math.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use LaTeX/MathJax with dollar signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Many posts at Mathematics Stack Exchange include mathematical notation, written using $\mathrm\LaTeX$ commands surrounded by dollar signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write mathematics using LaTeX commands and enclose them in dollar signs so MathJax can render them. Note: if you see dollar signs with what appears to be gibberish between them, it means MathJax isn't working for you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline formulas — single dollar signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Inline formulas are surrounded by single dollar signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from page: `$f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c` renders as $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$. Use single $...$ for expressions that appear within a line of text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block formulas — double dollar signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Block formulas are surrounded by double dollar signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from page: `$$x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac} }{2a}$$` renders on a separate line as the displayed formula. Use $$...$$ for larger expressions that should be displayed on their own line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greek letters via backslash names with capitalization by first letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Greek letters are mostly written by simply spelling them after a backslash with capitalization indicated by first letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: `\alpha \beta \Gamma \Delta` renders as α β Γ Δ. Use the backslash-name convention for Greek letters and capitalize the first letter for uppercase Greek symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the MathJax quick reference and additional pointers
rubrics_metrics.description: For a quick tutorial and command reference, see the MathJax quick reference page and additional pointers and references linked in the help center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided MathJax quick reference for commands and examples beyond the brief examples on this page. The help center links give more detailed tips and further resources for formatting mathematical notation correctly.
